description:
We are Intihuatana, a Peruvian team of five Software Engineering and Physical Sciences students passionate about science and innovation.

With Cosmic Legacy, we created an interactive platform featuring 3D models of NASA spacecraft, rovers and lunar modules, mission stories, quizzes, progress tracking and a resource-management simulation.

Available in two languages, our project makes space exploration engaging and accessible, inspiring young people to explore STEAM careers.
summary:
We have developed Cosmic Legacy, an interactive educational platform that allows users to explore the history of NASA rovers, space probes, and lunar modules through 3D models. It features Solar System visualizations, quizzes with progress tracking, a resource management simulation inspired by the Opportunity rover, and access in two languages.

Cosmic Legacy transforms complex scientific information into accessible, dynamic, and engaging learning experiences. Through 3D exploration, interactive activities, and decision-making, we bring users closer to space missions and the discoveries that have expanded our understanding of the universe.

The importance of our project lies in breaking down barriers that make science difficult to understand, especially for children and young people. We aim to demonstrate that learning science can be exciting and participatory, fostering curiosity, critical thinking, creativity, and innovation. We aspire to spark interest in STEAM careers and inspire future generations to become part of the next great scientific and technological discoveries.

WEBSITE FEATURES

Cosmic Legacy offers school-age students the opportunity to explore three-dimensional models of seven iconic pieces of space exploration equipment: Opportunity, Cassini, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10, Ingenuity, Surveyor 3, and the Apollo 11 Eagle lunar module. These models allow users to examine the equipment from different angles, understand its structure, and identify its main components, accompanied by descriptions explaining their characteristics and functions.

Through the "Explore Its History" section, users discover what each piece of equipment is, why it was sent into space, what its mission objectives were, and what discoveries or contributions it made to humanity's scientific knowledge. The information is presented through clear and accessible explanations adapted to the comprehension level of school-age students.

To reinforce learning, each story includes three interactive questions designed to assess users' understanding of the content they have explored. This approach is based on a learning technique known as Active Recall, which involves retrieving information from memory without directly referring to the studied material, helping improve comprehension and long-term retention.

In this way, Cosmic Legacy goes beyond the traditional presentation of scientific information: it transforms students into active participants in their own learning process. By combining three-dimensional exploration, scientific storytelling, and knowledge-retrieval activities, the platform aims to spark curiosity, encourage scientific thinking, and transform the study of space exploration into an engaging, interactive, and meaningful educational experience.

Interactive Solar System

In addition to the individual exploration of space equipment, Cosmic Legacy features an interactive 3D Solar System that allows users to explore the eight planets of our Solar System in a dynamic and visually engaging way.

Through this feature, students can select different planets, observe them from various perspectives, and zoom in to discover locations that have been explored through space missions. At the corresponding destinations, the platform displays interactive markers that identify the rovers, space probes, and lunar modules associated with different NASA missions.

By clicking on these markers, users can access information about the corresponding spacecraft, learn about its characteristics, explore its history, and discover the main scientific contributions of its mission.

This feature provides an alternative way to access the platform's educational content, complementing the individual exploration of space equipment. In this way, students not only learn about the instruments used in space missions but also connect them to the celestial bodies they explored, gaining a better understanding of each mission's context and its importance in expanding our knowledge of the universe.

Through this approach, Cosmic Legacy transforms navigation through the Solar System into an interactive learning and discovery experience, encouraging active participation, scientific curiosity, and a more visual and intuitive understanding of space exploration.

Expected Impact of Cosmic Legacy

Cosmic Legacy aims to create a positive educational and social impact by bringing space exploration and scientific knowledge closer to school-aged students through an interactive, accessible, and engaging web platform.

Our main goal is to spark scientific curiosity and inspire younger generations to pursue STEAM fields (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics), demonstrating that science can be understood in a simple, dynamic, and enjoyable way.

Through three-dimensional models of spacecraft and scientific instruments, users will be able to explore their structures, identify their components, and understand the significance of their missions and discoveries for humanity. Additionally, the platform incorporates questions based on the Active Recall learning method, which aims to strengthen comprehension and long-term knowledge retention.

In the long term, we aspire to contribute to the democratization of scientific knowledge by reducing barriers to accessing specialized information and promoting independent learning. We also envision Cosmic Legacy becoming a complementary educational resource for teachers and educational institutions.

Ultimately, our project seeks not only to share knowledge about space exploration but also to inspire a new generation of curious, critical thinkers who are motivated to explore, discover, and innovate.

Tools, Programming Languages, and Software Used

To develop Cosmic Legacy, our team used HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES Modules) to build the website's structure, design its interface, and implement interactive educational features, including the Solar System explorer, spacecraft information, quizzes, simulations, and progress tracking.

For 3D visualization, we used Google's <model-viewer> library, WebGL technology, and 3D models in glTF/GLB format. These technologies allow users to rotate, zoom in on, and examine spacecraft and celestial bodies directly in their browsers. We incorporated 3D resources from NASA and JPL, alongside simplified educational models of Apollo 11 and Surveyor 3 created with AI assistance.

Our main development environment was Visual Studio Code, using the Live Server extension for local testing. We also used GitHub for team collaboration and version control, while Cloudflare was used for web deployment.

Additionally, we used Google Fonts, specifically Cormorant Garamond and Manrope, to enhance the website's visual design. ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Gemini (Google) provided AI assistance during development, including programming, documentation, and educational content creation.

The platform uses browser local storage to save user progress without requiring accounts or a database. It runs directly in modern web browsers, making the educational experience accessible without additional software installation.

Originality of Our Project

Cosmic Legacy takes a creative approach to science education by transforming complex information about NASA's space missions into an interactive and engaging learning experience. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, users can examine 3D spacecraft models, discover their components, navigate an interactive Solar System, and explore the stories behind seven remarkable missions.

Our project also incorporates the Active Recall learning technique through interactive quizzes, encouraging students to reinforce their knowledge. By combining scientific storytelling, 3D visualization, and educational activities, Cosmic Legacy makes space exploration more accessible, memorable, and exciting for young learners.

Key Factors We Considered

Our team considered several key factors during the development of Cosmic Legacy, particularly educational accessibility, scientific accuracy, user engagement, and interactive learning.

We focused on presenting complex scientific concepts in clear, age-appropriate language so that school-age students could understand them without requiring advanced scientific knowledge. We also prioritized reliable information from NASA and JPL to ensure the educational content was scientifically grounded.

Additionally, we considered the importance of intuitive navigation, visually appealing 3D models, and bilingual accessibility in English and Spanish. Finally, we incorporated interactive activities to encourage active participation, strengthen knowledge retention, and inspire curiosity about science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics (STEAM).
